The test image shows a close-up of a soybean leaf with significant yellowing/chlorosis and a dark, nearly black lesion in the center. The lesion has a dense, dark coloration that could indicate fungal acervuli or pustules. The surrounding tissue is yellowed.

Top candidates: Anthracnose (dark acervuli), Frogeye_leaf_spot, or Soybean_rust (pustules). Let me check one reference.

The Anthracnose reference shows stem/pod symptoms (brown streaking), not matching the test image's leaf lesion pattern.

**Test image analysis:**
- Single, defined dark lesion (near-black/dark blue-brown) on a heavily chlorotic/yellow leaf
- Close macro shot showing the lesion has some textural structure
- Surrounding tissue is uniformly yellowed

The single circular dark lesion on a yellowed leaf is most consistent with **Frogeye_leaf_spot** (circular spots with dark center, leaf yellowing) or possibly Soybean_rust (dark uredinia). The lesion appears too localized/single for rust (which causes many scattered pustules). The dark, defined spot on yellowing tissue fits frogeye best.
